name: The Carcass Tours (Old Chicago Urbex Circuit)
description: An organized — and officially illegal — network of guided explorations into the pre-collapse infrastructure of Old Chicago buried beneath M88's Tier 1 foundations, known colloquially as 'the Carcass.' Unlike solitary urban explorers, Carcass Tours operate as curated experiences: guides called Anatomists lead groups of 4-8 through specific routes into flooded Loop-era transit tunnels, pre-collapse residential towers subsided into the lakebed fill, and the famous 'Millennium Pocket,' an air-stable pocket beneath what was once Millennium Park containing art installations from the 2020s still partially intact under decades of sediment. Tours are advertised through physical paper cards left in Tier 2 cafes and Shelf community boards — never digitally. The most sought-after Anatomist, known as Sorrow, claims to have mapped more than 60 kilometers of accessible Carcass routes over fifteen years.
cultural_impact: The Carcass Tours have cultivated a widespread popular mythology around Old Chicago as a sacred site of pre-corporate urban life — a place where you can touch something that existed before corponations owned everything. This mythology has political weight: several Shelf land-rights movements explicitly frame their arguments around the idea that M88 was built on ground that once belonged to people, not entities.
key_figures: Sorrow (master Anatomist, identity protected, believed to be Shelf-born)
Benedikt Achebe-Lindqvist (Tier 3 historian who has written the only academic paper on the tours)
Enforcement Captain Isolde Mwangi-Reyes (has arrested 14 tourists, never an Anatomist)
locations: The Millennium Pocket (subsurface air pocket beneath former Millennium Park)
Drowned Loop (flooded pre-collapse transit tunnels, Loop district subsurface)
Entry Point Vashti (best-known Carcass access point, Shelf Ward 9 basement)
story_hooks: A Carcass Tour group discovers a sealed room in the Drowned Loop containing active pre-collapse server hardware still drawing power from an unknown source — and the data on it is current, not historical.

Sorrow goes missing after a solo mapping run, and the only clue is a hand-drawn map card left at Entry Point Vashti showing a route that no other Anatomist recognizes — one that appears to go down, not across.

A corponation announces plans to 'stabilize and develop' the Carcass as a heritage tourism destination, and the Anatomists must decide whether to resist, collaborate, or destroy their own maps to prevent the routes from being commodified.
